name: Abernys: Port Covenant
notes: Built from the Abernys docs in the Howling Whispers dev project (region seed, Port Covenant, Fenmire, Cairn Maw). Anything marked canonStatus "draft" was invented to make the slice playable: every route distance, the district and building names, the gate staff and their Four Approaches tiers (the Arbiter a rival, the guard a minion), and the player character. Proposed names from the docs (the Governor, the High Arbiter, the garrison captain, Brond) are draft too. The calendar is the default real one until Abernys has its own.

world.name: Abernys
world.summary: A dark-fantasy island in the Bitterroot universe, a month or two's sail from Bitterroot, settled in layers of migration and conquest.

identity.name: Abernys
identity.description: An island of layered migrations: first peoples with no memory of arriving, later waves that migrated, conquered and mixed, and humans as the latest.

importantFacts: The first peoples are prey peoples; both conquests that followed were by predators. Humans are neither predator nor prey, so nobody on Abernys knows how to read them.

A plague called the Wailing struck every species, beginning at Nospier Point. Humans were immune and settled the half-empty city while everyone else kept away. Whether it came before the humans or with them is a deliberate mystery.
No one enters Port Covenant without signing the Covenant, and nothing binds a party until they sign.

rules.constraints: Fen witchcraft is ritual and alchemical; nothing about it is confirmed supernatural.

places.name: Abernys
places.description: The island. Its coast faces the open sea to the west, and every power on it is within a few days of Caerwyn.

places.name: Nospier Point
places.description: The southern headland. Its port city was the first and worst hit by the Wailing, and the immune humans settled it while the rest of Abernys kept away.

places.name: Port Covenant
places.description: The human colony inside its walls, where the Pact lives by the Covenant: everything is contracts and leverage, and nothing exists unless it is on paper. Most of the poor are indentured, which the Pact does not count as slavery because every party agreed.

places.name: The harbour
places.description: Smaller and harder to work than Caerwyn's, with temperamental weather, but richer fishing and fewer pirates. Shipwrights work the slips.

places.name: The Arbiters' registry
places.description: Where the Arbiters, a monastic order of notaries, make and keep the colony's paper. In a society this litigious, the people who keep the contracts hold real influence.

places.name: The garrison
places.description: Barracks of the colony's soldiers. Patrols go out from here to survey land, hunt runaways and guard diggers.

places.name: The Governor's court
places.description: Seat of the Governor, whose commission is the colony's claim to the land.

places.name: The landward gate
places.description: Where the headland road meets the colony wall. An Arbiter takes signatures at the gate, because no one enters the port without signing.

places.name: The outer lanes
places.description: Where most of the colony's mixed families live, in the lanes between the wall and the open headland.

places.name: Fenmire
places.description: Hard, wet fen and bog between the Woed and the south coast. Proud, independent first peoples (harefolk, badgerfolk and salamanders) live in private family clusters, where killing a trespasser is no crime.

places.name: Bogwater
places.description: The nearest thing Fenmire has to a town: the fen's trading post and the seat of the Council of Crones. Outsiders may trade here, under suspicion, and it is as far into the fen as most of them get.

places.name: Cairn Maw
places.description: Chalk uplands inland, held by three first-peoples clans who share a grievance and no government. High tension, no war.

places.name: The Aurochs downs
places.description: Clan Aurochs' downs, running south toward Port Covenant: thin chalk turf, lime kilns along the scarp and the great barrows. Colony patrols cross them, and the barrow-keepers kill diggers.

places.name: Caerwyn
places.description: The city-state at the mouth of the Afon's estuary, where sea trade and river trade meet. A figurehead ruler sits under the real power of merchants and organised crime.

requires.reason: No one enters the port without signing the Covenant.

routes.terrain: lanes along the outside of the wall
headland road, then fen causeways known to locals and easy for strangers to lose
chalk track up the scarp onto the downs
punt channels out of the fen, then the coast road; the fen traders' regular trek

species.name: Humans
species.description: The latest arrivals: colonizers at Port Covenant, thralls on the wreck coast, mudflat dwellers in Caerwyn.

species.name: Salamanders
species.description: First peoples of the fens. None appear among Bitterroot's peoples.

species.name: Cervidfolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Hart of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Caprinefolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Crag of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Bovinefolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Aurochs of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Foxfolk
species.description: Earlier migration from Bitterroot, by a route nobody remembers.

species.name: Wolves
species.description: Sea raiders turned rulers of the fjord jarldoms, and muscle among the pirates.

factions.name: The Arbiters
factions.description: A monastic order of notaries headed by the High Arbiter. They make and keep the Pact's paper and enforce the law alongside the Governor's court and the garrison.

societies.name: The Pact
societies.description: The humans of Port Covenant and the beastkin who have signed into it. A law applies only to those who sign it, no contract is unfair, and the most important contracts are tattooed on the body.

memories.title: The arrival
memories.description: Humans driven from the homeland by a disaster that stays unwritten settled the city the Wailing had emptied. How many generations ago is never stated.

characters.name: The traveller
characters.description: A traveller come up the headland road to Port Covenant, with no paper and no signature to their name.
characters.draftNote: Placeholder player character until an Orbis persona is chosen.

characters.name: The gate Arbiter
characters.description: An Arbiter on duty at the landward gate, with the Covenant's terms, ink, and a ledger of everyone who has signed.

characters.name: A garrison guard
characters.description: One of the garrison's soldiers, posted at the gate.

characters.name: Ottavio Marrane
characters.description: Leads the colony. Wants the homeland's silence kept from the colonists. His commission is the colony's claim to the land, and every document it rests on sits in the Arbiters' keeping.

characters.name: Lucan Abreu
characters.description: Heads the Arbiters. Wants every bargain on the coast written in the Pact's hand, and knows the Covenant only binds those who sign it.

characters.name: Ines Corvo
characters.description: Holds the colony's soldiers and best weapons. Wants the borders held, and keeps losing patrols in the clashes on the downs and in the fen.

characters.name: Cadfan
characters.description: A weathered badger with a punt and a Caerwyn buyer's mark on his barrels, on the regular trek between Bogwater and Caerwyn. Easier with outsiders than most fen folk, which is why he's useful and why the clusters don't fully trust him.

characters.name: Brond
characters.description: Wants war on Port Covenant. Has the most men and the great barrows; his barrow-keepers keep killing colony diggers, and every body brings a patrol.

terminals.note: They go down with an injury and take no further part in this scene.
They are spent: they give way, or can push no further.
The scene is roused: everyone present is alert and looking for trouble.

actions.name: Sign the Covenant
actions.summary: Put your name in the Arbiter’s ledger. From then on the Covenant binds you, and the gate is open to you.
actions.outcome: The player signs the Covenant in the Arbiter’s ledger. It binds them from this moment, and the landward gate is open to them.

scenario.title: At the landward gate
scenario.opening:
*Fog lies over Nospier Point. The headland road ends at a wall of dressed stone and a gate standing half open, a garrison guard leaning in its shadow. Under the arch an Arbiter has laid out ink, a pen and a ledger on a narrow table, and doesn't look up.*

"Name," she says, "and whether you can write it. No one goes through without signing."
